topic.title: Managing a Translation Job
topic.shortdesc: How to follow a running translation job, bring its results into your workspace, and manage it from the job card.

body.p: Whether you are translating a project for the first time or running an incremental update, you follow and manage every translation job the same way, from a card in your workspace.
Each translation job appears as a card. While the job is pending or running, the card shows the current step and a progress indicator, and you can stop the job from the card.
When a job finishes, select Bring into Workspace on the card to add its translated files to your workspace for review. The card's overflow menu lets you remove the job.

p.note: While a translation job is running, do not make other changes in the same workspace to the source or target files it covers. Concurrent edits can conflict with the files the agent is about to write, and the translation job does not track them.

section.title: Checking the Job Log
section.p: Every job that has started running keeps an execution log. Two controls on the card open it:

ul.li: View log - opens the Execution log dialog. While the job is running, the log updates live; after it finishes, it shows the final log.
Download log - saves the full log as a text file, for example to attach when you contact support.

section.p: The most common reason to open the log is to find out why a job failed. A failed job card shows only a short failure message, while the log records the underlying cause.
For example, a job fails when your organization has run out of AI credits, which the log reports as an AI credits exhausted error.

fig.title: Execution Log of a Failed Job

section.p: The log is also one of the two places the agent can put its answer when you ask it a question instead of asking it to translate.

section.title: Tracking Which Jobs You Have Brought In Your Workspace
section.p: When you have many finished jobs, it can be hard to tell which ones you have already brought into your workspace. After you select Bring into Workspace, the job is marked with an Integrated badge, and its tooltip shows when it was brought in.

If you need to bring the same job in again (for example, after you discarded the changes), select Mark as not integrated from the card's overflow menu. This clears the badge and restores the Bring into Workspace action.
